extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, marketers, communications teams, product managers launching new products
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing press releases announcing a new or updated product, covering structure, messaging, multimedia, timing, and distribution to maximize media pickup, SEO, and sales impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention-Grabbing Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should focus on what's new and exciting about your product rather than a bland announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it under 100 characters, use strong action verbs, and avoid vague buzzwords like 'game-changing.' Example given: instead of 'Company X Launches New Software,' write 'Company X Unveils AI-Powered Software That Cuts Design Time in Half.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Product Description (Lead Paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a concise overview in the first paragraph explaining what your product is and who can benefit from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the main value proposition and market need up front; save detailed specs for later paragraphs. Example: 'DesignPro AI helps graphic designers automate tasks, cutting completion time by 50%.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Features and Benefits Focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline specific customer benefits and how the product solves problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on three to five key features, start with the most compelling, and use specific numbers (e.g., time saved, efficiency gained). Include technical specs only if relevant to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Rich Multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Include high-resolution multimedia assets to help outlets visualize the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide product photos, screenshots, videos, infographics, logos and headshots. Lead with your strongest visual because some outlets may only use one image. Use infographics for complex features and video to show features in action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Call-to-Action (CTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell readers exactly what to do next (pre-order, purchase, learn more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place CTAs naturally within the release, include direct links to product pages, signup forms, social profiles, or sales contacts, make sure all links work, and offer promotions if driving immediate sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and emphasize unique features that set the product apart from competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how features directly benefit users and solve problems differently; stay focused on strengths without criticizing competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a Compelling Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Use storytelling to connect with the audience and explain why the product matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share why you created the product, what problems it solves, and weave in market trends and industry context. Keep language simple and skip technical jargon that might confuse readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Data Strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims with specific, credible data from research or testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share concrete results (e.g., 'Early users report 40% faster completion times') and choose the most impressive, verifiable stats; cite credible sources or studies where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Distribution Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Time the release to maximize coverage and avoid conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research industry events, competitor announcements, and seasonal factors; give journalists plenty of lead time for coverage and ensure the release is complete before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Use Cases for Product Press Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify when a product press release is the right format to announce news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations include introducing a completely new product, expanding a product line, adding major features/updates, entering new markets/regions, or relaunching/rebranding an existing product.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO Optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize the press release to improve search visibility for the product and announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relevant keywords and SEO-friendly phrasing so the release appears in search results; include links to product pages and other web assets to support discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes and Authority Building
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from executives or stakeholders to add authority and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a powerful quote that connects the product to the brand mission or market need; provide headshots when quotes are used to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia and Asset Prioritization for Outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize how outlets use assets and prioritize accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with your strongest visual because some outlets will only use one image. Provide a range of assets but ensure the primary photo or screenshot communicates the product clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template Use and Customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates can provide helpful structure but must be tailored to the product and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize standard sections (headline, product description, quotes, boilerplate) to highlight your unique value proposition rather than relying on generic copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate and Company Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a concise boilerplate that summarizes the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate clear and relevant to the product context; use it to reinforce credibility and provide quick background for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and Format Tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Study exemplary press releases for different product announcement types to learn effective approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt tactics from examples: brand-new product releases may balance technical detail with user benefits and partnerships; product line extensions should lead with market context and a founder quote; software feature announcements should simplify complex features and use video demos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Plain Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep prose clear, concise, and free of unnecessary jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make complex or technical points digestible for journalists and broader audiences; avoid overreliance on buzzwords that obscure meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and Practical Details
rubrics_metrics.description: State availability, market rollout, and any purchase/ordering information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include release dates, regions/markets served, pricing or promotional details when relevant so journalists and customers know how and when to access the product.
